title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO; Kress interim CEO; stock closes 4.3% lower; results 18 Nov IST (photo cover)
headline: Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia CEO After 33 Years. What Next? →
caption:
Nvidia is looking for a new CEO for the first time in its history. Jensen Huang resigned as president, CEO and board member on Thursday, 12 November, effective immediately. He co-founded the company in 1993 and led it for 33 years.

Chief financial officer Colette Kress is now interim CEO and keeps the CFO job. Harvey C. Jones becomes the first board chair in Nvidia's history, and the board will consider internal and external candidates for a permanent CEO.

Nvidia's announcement gives no reason and carries no statement from Huang. Earlier, on 8 November, the board had said independent directors were investigating reports that he was the target of a foreign intelligence effort.

The stock fell as much as 14% in early New York trade, to $148.80, and closed the day 4.3% lower, with Nvidia's market value ending just above $4 trillion. Nvidia makes up just over 6% of the S&P 500, an index that some Indian funds track.

Quarterly results are still due on 17 November US time: about 2:50 AM IST on 18 November, with the investor call at 3:30 AM IST.

Who should run Nvidia next: an insider or an outsider?

Sources: Nvidia (announcement and SEC filing), CNBC, ABC News, Yahoo Finance, CNN
